messages:
maria: Quick question — customer ACME says their S3 audit export contains internal_service_id and dev_notes fields. Want to confirm the contract for customer-facing events and plan a short schema prune.
jonah: Can you paste an example of the exported event? We should check schema version header and whether the anonymization step ran.
maria: Yep — snippet from their S3 object (redacted):
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-10-15T14:12:05Z",
  "event_type": "model.inference.request",
  "user_id": "acct_12345",
  "internal_service_id": "worker-gpu-42",
  "dev_notes": "repro: race on cache miss",
  "payload": { "tokens": 234 }
}
```
samir: internal_service_id + dev_notes definitely internal-only. We should add a deploy blocker: delivery pipeline must strip any fields listed as "internal" in schema v2.
jonah: Agree. Two things: 1) Add optional header in webhook/S3 metadata: X-Redwood-Audit-Version: 2 2) Validate during onboarding that customers have agreed to the output field set.
maria: For S3 exports, how do we signal the version to customers so old parsers don't break?
devex_ellen: Recommend adding a top-level "schema_version" string in each event and an "export_metadata.json" file in each export prefix that enumerates field visibility + pseudonymization rules. That way we don't rely on object keys alone.
samir: Also propose a small transform layer in the delivery service: a whitelist filter by schema_version before writing to S3 or sending webhooks. That makes it explicit and deterministic.
jonah: For webhooks, we already send signature headers: X-Redwood-Signature and X-Redwood-Timestamp. Plan: add X-Redwood-Audit-Version and X-Redwood-Pseudonymization (enum: none, pseudonymize, redact). Example webhook header set: 
```
X-Redwood-Audit-Version: 2
X-Redwood-Pseudonymization: pseudonymize
X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=...
```
maria: How do we handle field-level RBAC changes? e.g., platform admins vs customer-admins see different user identifiers.
samir: Field-level RBAC should be resolved at the delivery boundary. The delivery runtime needs the tenant contract (enum) and role mapping; then apply transform: keep full_user_id for internal tenants, pseudonymize for customer-admin, redact for public exports.
devex_ellen: I'll add a checklist item for onboarding docs: include sample postman for webhook validation and an example S3 export with export_metadata.json.
maria: One more — Splunk/Datadog users asked about timestamp formats and nested arrays not being flattened. We should include a mapping doc and a small adapter for Splunk HEC that converts nested fields into dotted keys.
jonah: Good call. Also add a test harness to the onboarding flow: customer provides a small synthetic event set; our validation job runs and returns a compatibility report (fields stripped, signature verified, KMS envelope OK).
security-bot: Incident INC-1234 linked: found 3 S3 exports missing schema_version in last 24h. Assigned to @maria.
maria: I'll take INC-1234. Plan: patch delivery to add schema_version and export_metadata.json by EOD, then run compatibility job for ACME.
samir: For KMS: ensure the envelope has proper key rotation headers (x-kms-key-id) and include a field in export_metadata.json: "kms_envelope": "rsa-oaep-sha256".
devex_ellen: I'll update the onboarding playbook and add a short sample JSON for export_metadata in the docs repo.
jonah: After we ship, we'll run a sweep to find any historical exports missing "schema_version" and backfill an export_metadata.json with default visibility rules.
maria: Thanks all. Tagging follow-ups: @devex_ellen to update docs, @samir to make transform patch, @jonah to add compatibility job, I'll handle incident and customer comms. :thumbsup:
